       self-hosted Linux compiler eb57aa4d7a3c1317caf5921a6ddabf7b
ppcx64.exe md5:    293F3C98A26FF3233D88550259BA8B1F
ppcx64.exe sha256: A5B6CEF78FF5E80943794694BDD78D1DC21A34C7BAD4D1734EA53167F0AFDA06

Change in this release -- inferred types for inline vars:

1. An untyped INTEGER initialiser now infers NativeInt (= PtrInt) instead of the
   hard-coded LongInt.  `var i := -1` used to be 4 bytes on every target; it is
   now pointer-width, so 8 bytes on a 64-bit app and still 4 on a 32-bit one.
   The same rule applies to an inferred for-loop counter (`for var i := 0 ...`),
   so the two cannot disagree.
   Only types strictly NARROWER than NativeInt are widened, so Int64/QWord keep
   their width and no value is ever lost or re-signed.  An explicit typecast is
   still never touched: `var b := byte(10)` stays a byte.

2. A STRING or CHAR literal initialiser now infers exactly what a bare `string`
   denotes at that point (the compiler shares one helper with the `string`
   keyword, so they cannot drift apart).  Under -Mdelphiunicode and -Munleashed
   that is the wide/unicode string -- which is what the directive asks for, and
   what those two modes already produced before this release.  The behaviour
   that genuinely changes is $H-, where inference used to hand back a dynamic
   wide string even though `string` there means ShortString.

Distribution requirements:
- This is a COMPILER-BINARY-ONLY refresh on top of the v53 release.
  Only compiler/defutil.pas and compiler/pstatmnt.pas changed since v53.
  No PPU format change, no RTL change, no package change.
- Pair with vibepascal-v52-win64-units.tar.gz (the v52 1803-PPU unit set, still
  current -- v53 and v54 are both binary-only refreshes on top of it).  Existing
  v52/v53 unit installs stay valid and do NOT need re-pulling.
- Install through C:\Lazarus\auto-update.bat.

Validation (all performed by me on x86_64-linux, against a baseline compiler
built from the parent commit, md5 23618ea0680578c23f16059b58b71757):
- tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp -- 45 assertions over 13 structural
  contexts: free procedure, method, nested begin..end, nested procedure,
  with-block, inferred for-loop counter, try/finally/except bodies,
  while/repeat/case bodies, explicit typecasts, wide (u32/s64) literals,
  non-literal right-hand sides (vars, function results, untyped consts,
  expressions), non-integer kinds (boolean/double/pointer/enum) and the MAIN
  PROGRAM BODY.  Baseline 26 failures -> 0.  Under BOTH -Munleashed AND
  -Mdelphiunicode.
- tests/test/tinlinevarstrinfer1.pp -- 20 assertions across $H+ and $H-, each
  checked against what `var s: string` yields in the same spot.  Baseline 4
  failures (all in the $H- section) -> 0.  Both modes.
- Full corpus tests/test, 2098 tests, compile code + run code + output hash,
  with a baseline-vs-baseline control run to identify the 17 tests that are
  nondeterministic (threading/atomics).  19 raw deltas - 17 nondeterministic =
  3 real deltas, and all 3 are the intended tests flipping fail -> pass.
  ZERO unintended regression.  The 17 nondeterministic tests were additionally
  checked to have UNCHANGED compile results, so the noise hides nothing.
- Self-host fixpoint: stage B == stage C byte-identical
  (cb5ca5e9adb2b95f7d1ccc98ac0bc6c5); the shipped Linux compiler
  eb57aa4d7a3c1317caf5921a6ddabf7b is the same compiler built through the
  canonical make path and differs from it in 6 build-date bytes only.

NOT verified on this host: Win64 RUNTIME behaviour. This box is Linux with no
wine installed, so the .exe is PE32+-verified and cross-built from the identical
source commit, but it has never been executed.  The first runtime proof is the
auto-update.bat smoke on a Windows host.

Compatibility note -- this is a deliberate semantic change, so code that relies
on an inferred integer being exactly 4 bytes will notice.  An inline var passed
to a `var LongInt` parameter, or one whose overload choice depended on LongInt,
now selects the NativeInt/Int64 shape instead.  Write the type explicitly
(`var i: longint := -1`) where the narrow width is load-bearing.
